trust_decision.summary: A2DP decides how many remote SEPs from a peer's AVDTP Discover response it stores in the fixed 10-entry global table; at the pinned commit every matching, not-in-use SEP is appended with no bound check.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'A2DP SEP discovery out-of-bounds write'. The only SEP-discovery array write in A2DP is in the AVDTP_SUBEVENT_SIGNALING_SEP_FOUND case, and the published fix lands there.

fix_sites.entry_point: a2dp_config_process_avdtp_event_handler (reached from the a2dp_source/a2dp_sink packet handlers) for AVDTP_SUBEVENT_SIGNALING_SEP_FOUND. That event is emitted by avdtp_signaling_emit_sep (src/classic/avdtp_util.c:638-651) for each entry of a remote Discover accept response, parsed in src/classic/avdtp_initiator.c:194-206
fix_sites.module_kind: protocol profile layer (A2DP config process over AVDTP), library code

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No second route to dismiss. The only nearby choice is fixing in the lower layer: capping SEP emission in avdtp_initiator.c:194-206 would also close the bug, but it is the same single route.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: SEPs that are in use or of the wrong type must still be skipped without using a slot. Discovery must still finish with the first 10 matching SEPs (SEP_DISCOVERY_DONE, then AVDTP_SI_DISCOVER accept leads to get_all_capabilities). A fix that rejects or aborts the whole discovery when there are more than 10 SEPs would break connections to peers with many endpoints. The count==0 path that ends discovery must also be kept.

O6_input_shapes: Discover accept response listing more than AVDTP_MAX_SEP_NUM (10) matching, not-in-use SEPs; the parser accepts up to the L2CAP payload size, with SEIDs 1..0x3E and duplicates allowed (src/classic/avdtp_initiator.c:194-205)

O7_producer.where: src/classic/avdtp_initiator.c:191-213 (Discover response parser, which emits one SEP_FOUND per 2-byte entry)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The SEID list of an incoming Suspend/Start command is copied into connection->suspended_seids[AVDTP_MAX_NUM_SEPS]. The bound `num_suspended_seids < AVDTP_MAX_NUM_SEPS` exists today, and dropping it in our copy would create a second sink in another file.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the same 'remote list into a fixed 10-slot table' idiom with a sibling constant (AVDTP_MAX_NUM_SEPS, src/classic/avdtp.h:62 and :617), on the acceptor side rather than the initiator/A2DP side. This is the 'role/direction variant' kind that lessons-v2 rates as weak.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The delay-reporting capability writes to seps[discovery_index]. Index safety depends only on the index/count bookkeeping at src/classic/a2dp.c:805-807 and the assert at :413.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A maintainer refactoring the capability loop could advance the index before the bound check. The resulting write sits in another event case, away from the SEP_FOUND write.

O9_family: memory safety: out-of-bounds write into a fixed-size global array; peer-controlled element count with no capacity check (CWE-787/CWE-1284)

O10_build.toolchain: gcc/clang with make or CMake; CppUTest for unit tests (test/avdtp_util/Makefile, test/avdtp_util/CMakeLists.txt)
O10_build.project_tests: test/avdtp_util has avdtp_util_test.cpp, avdtp_acceptor_test.cpp and codec_serialization_test.c. There is no a2dp test at the pinned commit; the fix adds test/avdtp_util/a2dp_test.cpp, which stubs AVDTP and feeds 11 SEP_FOUND events (fix.diff:62-206).

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add `if (count < AVDTP_MAX_SEP_NUM)` before the append at src/classic/a2dp.c:578. This is correct and complete; the main wrong alternative is aborting discovery entirely.

out_of_scope_notes: avdtp_initiator.c Discover parser (src/classic/avdtp_initiator.c:194-205) emits an unbounded number of SEP_FOUND events and accepts duplicate SEIDs. This is not a separate sink, only the producer.
